title: Loss of consortium claims - an underused head of compensation
p1:
A serious injury does not only affect the person who is hurt.

Sometimes, the biggest impact is felt by the person standing beside them.

Yet many people never consider claiming for that loss.
p2:
A common misconception is that compensation only covers medical bills, lost income, and physical pain. In reality, some legal systems recognize loss of consortium claims, which address the damage an injury causes to a spouse’s or family relationship.

The surprising part? The harm may include the loss of companionship, emotional support, affection, and the ability to share normal aspects of life together.
p3:
This head of compensation reminds us that injuries are not only financial events; they can change relationships and daily living. A strong claim requires showing how the injury affected the relationship, not just the physical condition of the injured person.

The practical takeaway: when evaluating compensation after a serious injury, look beyond visible losses and consider the personal impact on loved ones too.
conclusion: Have you seen loss of consortium claims being overlooked in injury cases, and do you think this area receives enough attention?
